title: Before a push, the guard checks the Red-run line on each test commit it sends
why: Incident, lane page-reply-uncollapse, 2026-11-07 03:30 CST, relayed by the coordinator 03:27 CST: test-file commit 1f35b617 was pushed with no `Red-run:` line. The gap showed only at `merge --lane-lint`, after the push, so the only fix was a replacement PR for #1345. Second incident, lane pr-state-is-on-the-pr, 2026-11-07 13:28 CST: commit af063548b was pushed to report-pass-needs-record with a malformed `Red-run:` line, because check_red_run ran after the push. The fix needed a new branch, since a force push is the owner's act. So the guard must also refuse a malformed line, not only a missing one.
note: Before a `git push`, the guard runs lint/check_red_run.py against the base for the commits the push sends. Cost: one git log and one diff read per push. Depends on step commit-refuses-conflict-markers, which builds the push-time check of the sent commits; this step extends that same home (building-one-home-per-capability). Done check: a red test on a push of a test commit with no Red-run line. The guard's verdict changes, so this is a build lane (test-author, builder, reviewer). No owner question. Absorbs proposed step red-run-at-commit (lane notes-fix-large-3, 18:04 CST Nov 7): 58bc56a3b and 435bafefb were pushed with `Red-run: none (...)`, a revert did not clear it, and #1631/#1632 replaced #1535/#1605. A push-time check stops that form before it lands; add a test that `Red-run: none (x)` is refused and `Red-run: none: x` allowed. Incident, Nov 7 23:14 CST (lane notes-fix-page, session_013NEJKzjkypcToggneCjJN8): a comment edit to a test file was pushed with no Red-run trailer (404b68a67 on #1482). Lane lint caught it only after the push, so the fix needed replacement PR #1785. Open PR #1582 (Refuse a push that sends a test commit with no valid Red-run trailer) builds this guard. Sighting (lane silent-undo-reads-retire-run, 04:50 CST Nov 8): db10b8d6b committed a test-file edit with no Red-run line, and only CI's check_red_run would have caught it. It forced #1911 to replace #1907. Step red-run-at-commit (a commit-time hook) is folded here (coordinator, 04:51 CST Nov 8); lane verdict-instruction-false-alarm (session_013NEJL1BCgLVUACYU5ujv9A) does not build it. That lane's #1376 sighting also belongs here; triage asked the lane for its detail. #1376 sighting (lane verdict-instruction-false-alarm, 04:52 CST): cfbd31c9 reworded two comment lines in hooks/test_guard.py with no Red-run trailer and was pushed; lane-lint's Red-run step (lint/check_red_run.py) caught it after a test-author flagged it. Auto mode refused both force-push forms that would fix it, so the lane opened replacement PR #1913 (third case under note lane-force-push-refused). #1949 sighting (lane revive-1042, 06:50 CST Nov 8): a comment-only edit to hooks/test_guard.py was pushed with no `Red-run: none:` trailer; lane-lint caught it after the push, and auto mode refused the force push to fix it. Same shape as #1376; the lane's other idea, a commit-time ask for the trailer, is this step's commit-side check. Third sighting (lane lint-before-record-push, 08:15 CST Nov 8; proposed step red-run-trailer-at-commit, folded here): #1898 commit 1d1067f82 added test lines with no Red-run trailer, caught only at lane lint; once pushed, only a replacement PR fixed it (#2032 replaces #1898). Sighting (lane fix-none-cite-check, session_013NEJL2ChVc4QiMs2icnEB8, 09:20 CST Nov 8): comment-only commit 3dcbac488 touched a test file with no Red-run line; check_red_run caught it only at `merge --lane-lint`, after the push, so #2051 became #2088 and #2082 became #2089. Its proposed step red-run-at-commit was already folded here (coordinator, 04:51 CST Nov 8). Two more sightings, Nov 8: (1) lane agent-report-shas-resolve 13:10 CST, proposed step red-run-at-commit again: comment-only commit 576ec5b5c on #1864 had no Red-run trailer; auto mode denied the force push to fix it, so the work moved to replacement PR #2235 and the review records split across two PRs. (2) Lane lint-before-record-push 13:10 CST: the code-check comment rule caught test comments that cite rulings and dates twice in one lane (#1898, #2032); only the lane lint caught them, so the commit-side checks should run it too.
